name: Fortify Health (HLI, 2024)
summary: Works with flour mills in India to fortify wheat flour with iron. The Happier Lives Institute's estimate of the wellbeing effects of Fortify Health's open-market programme over 2025–27 (WELLBYs per $1,000), rebuilt from the figures in its report.

source.title: Ironing out wellbeing: a shallow exploration into the wellbeing cost-effectiveness of fortifying wheat with iron (Fortify Health)
source.license: © Happier Lives Institute; no licence published. Numbers cited as facts with their source.

resources.title: HLI, How iron fortification impacts happiness: a charity evaluation of Fortify Health (2024)
resources.note: HLI publishes no public spreadsheet for this estimate: the model is built from the inputs and figures stated in the report's text, each quoted on its row. Its calculation sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/16WypWBxCXP3-QtP4o-H09XR_JinDqMoP445Lot-ACUs) asks for sign-in.

sections.title: HLI's totals for the next three years (report Table 10)
Discounting
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not HLI's. HLI counts a year of better wellbeing the same whenever it comes. In our view, later years count less at the discount rate under Your values, as in GiveWell's models; the evaluator view sets the rate to 0, so HLI's figure is unchanged there.

sections.title: Staff pay below market
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not the evaluator's: with credit by share of resources on, staff's pay below what they could earn elsewhere counts as an in-kind contribution and gets its share of the outcome. Off by default.

rows.label: WELLBYs from less anaemia while eating fortified flour (2025–27 average)

source.title: HLI report
source.quote: Total WELLBYs from concurrent anaemia benefits | 33,853.21

rows.explainer: People who are anaemic (40% of the population in India) gain about 0.01 WELLBYs for each year they eat fortified flour (6 studies linking anaemia and depression, 5 trials of fortification and anaemia).

rows.label: WELLBYs for children exposed to more iron in the womb (2025–27 average)
rows.explainer: About 68,000 pregnant women among the people served; HLI takes 2.99 WELLBYs per child from one trial of iron in pregnancy with a 12-year follow-up (60 mg a day), and cuts it to 0.38 for the much lower dose in flour (0.25) and for replication (0.51).

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000, including pregnancy effects
rows.explainer: HLI's figure for the open-market programme, averaged over 2025–27, on expenditure of $3.19 million a year. The two totals above divided by that expenditure give 23.4; HLI's table shows 22.79, presumably an average of the three years' ratios, and that is the number used here.

rows.label: Adjustment for possible harm of extra iron to people who are not anaemic

source.title: HLI report
source.quote: Adjustment for negative effects on healthy | 0.95

rows.explainer: HLI's "small subjective adjustment representing a 5% discount", for weak evidence that extra iron harms children who aren't deficient.

rows.label: WELLBYs per $1,000
rows.explainer: HLI: "we estimate Fortify Health's cost-effectiveness over the next three years to be 22 WELLBYs per $1,000 donated (WBp1k)" (21.65 in Table 10). HLI expects it to rise towards 39 to 68 as Fortify Health spends less on bringing in new mills.

rows.label: Discount rate on future wellbeing
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). HLI doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Share of the WELLBYs from exposure in the womb
rows.explainer: The less-anaemia benefit comes in the year the flour is eaten; the benefit to children exposed in the womb comes over their childhood.

rows.label: Years until the benefit to children exposed in the womb arrives, on average
rows.explainer: Our judgment: HLI's figure comes from a trial that followed children to age 12, so we place the benefit at the middle of those years, 6, with the whole span as the range.

rows.label: Discount factor
rows.explainer: The concurrent benefit isn't discounted; the in-womb benefit is discounted over the years until it arrives.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Fortify Health supplies millers with premix and dosing equipment for free and spends much of its budget bringing in new mills (HLI, section 4); staff are a minority of the cost. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Nonprofit staff in India often earn somewhat less than in comparable private-sector jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: WELLBYs per dollar
rows.explainer: The figure per dollar above; with credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
